newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish royal palace guard fires on colleagues.
newsitem.headline: Swedish royal palace guard fires on colleagues.

text.p: A Swedish soldier opened fire on his colleagues outside Stockholm's royal palace on Sunday and wounded two soldiers with the same bullet, police said.
The shooting took place moments before the changing of the palace guard, a ceremony usually popular with tourists, but freezing temperatures meant that only a few people were present.
Witnesses said they saw the soldier aim his A5 automatic rifle from the palace down over ramparts towards a group of soldiers approaching for the ceremony.
A police spokesman said the soldier had been arrested and neither of the two injured men -- an army captain and a national service soldier -- had suffered life-threatening injuries.
The captain was hit in the buttock by the bullet, which passed through his body and hit the other soldier standing nearby in the foot.
The royal palace, which dominates central Stockholm at the heart of the medieval old city, is used only for ceremonial purposes and the country's royal family lives elsewhere.
Johan Medin, captain of the royal palace guards, told reporters the soldiers' guns should not even be loaded as they were for ceremonial use only.
